Theme 016 · Typography & graphic systems

Proofreader's Redline

Your metrics are set like a galley proof: fine serif type, wide margins, line numbers. Pulse is the proofreader with a coral pen — it strikes the wrong figure, writes the right one above it and leaves a margin note — and a human initials the change in teal.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Galley page — warm white sheet, slug line, line numbers and a ruled left margin; type in Instrument Serif.
  • Strike & replace — a jittered coral line through the wrong figure, the corrected one written above in italic.
  • Circle — a loose hand-drawn loop around one word or action; never more than three marks per shot.
  • Margin note — italic coral annotation in the right margin with a thin leader line to the mark.
  • Metric table — typeset rows with mono figures, set like a financial page.
  • Human initials — a teal boxed sign-off ("✓ OK — on-call, 09:48") that closes each decision.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Pen stroke — stroke-dashoffset with slight speed variance, power2.out, 250–500 ms per mark, each mark starting on a beat at 120 BPM.
  • Value swap — the wrong figure dims to 30% while the correction masks up from below (200 ms), landing on the downbeat.
  • Margin pull — the leader draws in 180 ms, then the note fades in with a 1° rotation settle (back.out, 300 ms).

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

A red pen on a proof is the most exact picture of "review": the machine points at the mistake, the person decides and signs. It stays calm, editorial and very readable in a square. Risk: too many marks become chaos — cap it at three per shot and keep the page mostly clean.

Adapt to your product: typeset your own table (orders, test results, KPIs, contract terms) and let the pen correct one figure; the initials box is where your product's approve / reject action lives.
